client.name: OpenCode
client.auth: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from owner auth.json injected into child env only; no credential copied to profiles, repo, or logs

model_tool_catalog.evidence: captured OpenAI-compatible request body at the local instrumentation endpoint

arm_r.semantic_raw_call_test: rejected: No tool named "riltra_riltra_code_semantic" is currently available

health_probe.server_mode: pre-warmed local serve on 127.0.0.1:28994, then run --server

probe.command: Get-Location; Get-Command riltra; Test-Path Env:RILTRA_HOME; Test-Path .\riltra-home

limitations: OpenCode still watches C:\ProgramData for location events; no system config was found or loaded.
OPENCODE_CONFIG_PROJECT_DISABLE=1 did not stop project location detection; the pinned snapshot contains no project config.
opencode debug config without a per-profile service port can attach to the operator managed service; benchmark runs therefore use --standalone or an explicit pre-warmed --server.

methodology_deviations: The v2 permission mechanism that actually removes a tool from the model catalog is the permission map ({"tool": "deny"}), not the permissions array documented for MCP servers. The array left all 12 tools visible.
The Riltra MCP server still advertises 12 tools at the JSON-RPC protocol level. The model catalog exposes 11; a raw call to riltra_riltra_code_semantic is rejected by OpenCode.
RILTRA_LSP_SERVER is unset, so even a direct semantic call would fail with no language server configured.

A cold opencode run sends its first provider request before the MCP connection completes; that request has no Riltra tools. A pre-warmed serve (MCP connected) removes the race. The frozen prompts were not changed or run.
The catalog evidence uses a local OpenAI-compatible capture endpoint in place of DeepSeek; it captures the exact request body OpenCode would send. The real-model probes use DeepSeek.

The executed Arm R probes used a pre-warmed serve on 127.0.0.1:28994 and run --server; the executed Arm B isolation probe used run --standalone. Isolation is valid, but startup equivalence is not yet demonstrated for Arm B.
The catalog request contains two built-in OpenCode skills (opencode, report); no operator skill is present and the R/B directory skill sources are empty. The run is not zero-skill.
An R profile log records a separate OpenCode process (run=89f86d92) at 05:13 that queried the repository from its location service; it is not one of the three evidence sessions.
